Reporting confirmed incidents to customers, regulators, and other required parties satisfies IR-6(b).
Notifying customers and authorities of incidents is one form of communicating with external parties about matters affecting internal control.
Internal escalation and external notification are part of responding to identified incidents.

controls.name: Post-Incident Review
controls.summary: Conduct a documented post-incident review for significant incidents and track the resulting improvements to closure.
controls.statement: Complete a documented post-incident review within {{ review_deadline }} of resolving each incident rated {{ review_severity_threshold }}, identifying root cause and contributing factors, and track the resulting corrective actions to closure, including updates to incident response procedures, training, and testing.
controls.objective: Prevent recurrence of incidents and continuously improve detection, response, and recovery capability.
controls.guidance: Use a blameless postmortem template covering timeline, impact, root cause, detection gaps, and what went well. File corrective actions in the engineering backlog with owners and due dates and review open items in a recurring security meeting. Feed real incident scenarios into the next tabletop exercise (OGRL-IR-01) and update runbooks and detection rules. Evidence is the completed review linked to the incident record and the closed corrective-action tickets.

mappings.summary: Post-incident reviews with tracked corrective actions feed lessons learned into procedures, training, and testing as IR-4(c) requires.
Root-cause analysis and tracked improvements after incidents support recovery and prevention of recurrence.

controls.name: Privacy Breach Handling and Notification
controls.summary: Assess incidents involving personal information for harm and notification obligations, notify affected individuals and regulators on time, and record each breach.
controls.statement: For each incident involving personal information, follow the breach-response procedure in the incident response plan to assess the data and individuals affected, the likely harm to them, and available mitigations; determine notification obligations under {{ applicable_privacy_requirements }}; notify affected individuals and regulators within {{ breach_notification_deadline }} when required; and record the breach, harm assessment, and notification decision in {{ breach_register }}.
controls.objective: Ensure breaches of personal information are evaluated for harm, mitigated, and reported to affected individuals and authorities as legally and contractually required.
controls.guidance: Maintain a jurisdiction matrix of breach notification rules (for example GDPR 72-hour supervisory-authority notice, US state breach laws, HIPAA, and customer DPAs) and involve privacy counsel in every assessment. Consider data sensitivity, encryption status, and likelihood of misuse when assessing harm, and offer mitigations such as forced credential resets or credit monitoring where appropriate. Record decisions not to notify with their rationale. Where the organization acts as a processor, notify the controlling customer rather than individuals directly.

applicable_privacy_requirements.label: Applicable privacy and breach notification requirements
applicable_privacy_requirements.value: applicable privacy and breach notification laws, regulations, and customer contracts

breach_notification_deadline.label: Breach notification deadline
breach_notification_deadline.value: the shortest applicable legal or contractual deadline

mappings.summary: The documented breach procedure covers notification determination, harm assessment and mitigation, and applicable privacy requirements, and additionally requires executing notifications.
The breach register keeps a record of detected or reported breaches of personal information.
Timely breach notification to affected individuals and regulators addresses the notification aspect of this criterion.

controls.name: DoD Cyber Incident Reporting (DFARS 252.204-7012)
controls.summary: Report cyber incidents affecting covered defense information to DoD via DIBNet within 72 hours, submit malware to DC3, preserve forensic images and capture data for 90 days, and support DoD forensic analysis.
controls.statement: Designate {{ dod_reporting_roles }} to report cyber incidents to DoD, ensure they hold a valid DoD-approved medium assurance certificate, and verify certificate validity {{ certificate_check_frequency }}. When a cyber incident is discovered that affects a covered contractor information system or the covered defense information residing on it, or that affects the ability to provide operationally critical support: review affected and potentially accessed systems for evidence of compromise of covered defense information, including compromised computers, servers, specific data, and user accounts; report the incident to DoD at https://dibnet.dod.mil within 72 hours of discovery with the minimum required report elements; submit any malicious software discovered and isolated in connection with the reported incident to the DoD Cyber Crime Center (DC3) as DC3 or the Contracting Officer instructs; preserve and protect images of all known affected information systems and all relevant monitoring and packet capture data for at least 90 days from submission of the report; and, upon DoD request, provide access to additional information or equipment necessary for forensic analysis and provide the damage assessment information gathered.
controls.objective: Meet DFARS 252.204-7012 cyber incident obligations so DoD is informed in time and has the evidence it needs to assess damage to covered defense information.
controls.guidance: DFARS 252.204-7012 defines "rapidly report" as within 72 hours of discovery, so start the clock at discovery, not at confirmation of impact, and file an initial report with the information available and update it later. The report is filed through the DIBNet portal and must include the minimum elements listed there; access requires a DoD-approved medium assurance certificate, which can take weeks to obtain, so acquire certificates for more than one reporter before any incident and track their expiry. Capture forensic images (for example EBS or managed-disk snapshots, endpoint images, or memory captures) and export relevant SIEM, flow log, and packet capture data to a retention-locked location before rebuilding systems, and keep them at least 90 days after the report is submitted so DoD can request the media or decline interest. Submit malware to DC3 only as DC3 or the Contracting Officer instructs, never to the Contracting Officer. Where a cloud service provider hosts covered defense information, confirm it is contractually bound to the same reporting, preservation, and access obligations. Flow the clause down to subcontractors that handle covered defense information; they report directly to DoD and give the incident report number to the prime or next higher-tier subcontractor as soon as practicable. Record the DIBNet report number and submission time in the incident record.

certificate_check_frequency.label: Medium assurance certificate validity check frequency

dod_reporting_roles.label: Personnel responsible for DoD incident reporting
dod_reporting_roles.value: the security lead and at least one designated alternate

mappings.summary: Covers reporting incidents to DoD as the designated external authority; tracking, documentation, and other internal and external reporting come from OGRL-IR-03 and OGRL-IR-04.
Reports cyber incidents to DoD, one of the IR-6(b) authorities, and adds DFARS preservation, malware submission, and forensic access duties that IR-6 does not require.

controls.name: Centralized Security Audit Logging and Retention
controls.summary: Capture security-relevant authentication, authorization, and administrative logs centrally with tamper-resistant retention.
controls.statement: Log {{ logged_events }} across all in-scope systems to a centralized, access-controlled log store, review logging coverage {{ logging_review_cadence }}, and retain audit records for at least {{ retention_period }}.
controls.objective: Maintain reliable, tamper-resistant audit trails sufficient for forensic investigation and accountability.
controls.guidance: Synchronize system clocks via NTP, enforce append-only or write-once storage policies on log buckets, and ensure log shippers alert on ingestion drops.

logged_events.label: Auditable security event types
logged_events.value: authentication attempts, privilege changes, configuration mutations, and sensitive data access

tests.name: Verify Centralized Audit Logging Ingestion and Retention
tests.description: Confirm audit logging is enabled across all production accounts, logs flow into the central store, and bucket retention policies meet or exceed the configured minimum.

mappings.summary: Centralized security logging and retention satisfy ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.15.
Central logging of privilege changes and configuration mutations helps capture privileged function execution in audit logs; defining and blocking privileged functions are out of scope.
Specifies logged event types and creates and retains audit records, but does not define the required content of each record.
Central logging of authentication and privileged activity supports tracing actions to users, but the control does not require records to contain the user identity.
Reviews logging coverage on a defined cadence, but does not explicitly require logged event types to be updated from that review.
Centralized security event logging and review directly satisfy SP 800-171 03.03.01.
Centralized tamper-resistant retention directly satisfies NIST AU-11 audit record retention.
Centralized logging defines and captures auditable security event types per AU-2(a).
Periodic review of logged event scope directly satisfies NIST AU-2(e).
Centralized security audit logging supplies telemetry required for SOC 2 CC7.2 monitoring.

controls.name: Continuous Security Monitoring and Alert Triage
controls.summary: Monitor telemetry continuously for anomalous behavior and route high-severity security alerts for timely triage.
controls.statement: Continuously monitor system and security telemetry using {{ monitoring_methods }} to detect {{ monitoring_objectives }}, routing actionable alerts to {{ alert_recipients }} for triage within {{ triage_sla }}.
controls.objective: Detect unauthorized activity, intrusion attempts, and security anomalies quickly enough to contain impact.
controls.guidance: Tune SIEM/EDR rules to minimize alert fatigue, document escalation runbooks, and test alerting pipelines periodically.

monitoring_methods.label: Detection techniques and tools
monitoring_methods.value: automated SIEM correlation rules and cloud threat detection

monitoring_objectives.label: Security monitoring objectives
monitoring_objectives.value: unauthorized access, privilege escalation, malware execution, and anomalous data egress

tests.name: Verify Active Threat Detection and Alert Routing
tests.description: Confirm threat detection rules are active, alert delivery channels are healthy, and open high-severity alerts are triaged within SLA.

mappings.summary: Security telemetry monitoring contributes to boundary communication monitoring; defining boundaries and controlling and protecting traffic are out of scope.
Continuously monitors systems to detect attacks, but does not explicitly require monitoring of inbound and outbound communications traffic.
Detection of unauthorized access and privilege escalation identifies unauthorized use, but authorized use is not defined.
Continuous telemetry monitoring against defined threat objectives satisfies NIST SI-4(a.1).
SIEM correlation and cloud threat detection identify unauthorized system use per SI-4(b).
Routing actionable security alerts to on-call responders satisfies NIST SI-4(g).
Continuous security monitoring and anomaly detection satisfy SOC 2 CC7.2.

controls.name: Audit Log Protection
controls.summary: Store audit logs immutably with restricted access and alert on attempts to tamper with logging.
controls.statement: Store audit logs in {{ log_store }} with immutable or write-once retention, restrict read access to {{ log_reader_roles }}, prevent modification or deletion by any user including administrators of the logged systems, and alert {{ log_tamper_alert_recipients }} on attempts to disable logging, change log configuration, or delete log data.
controls.objective: Preserve the integrity and confidentiality of audit trails so they remain trustworthy for investigations.
controls.guidance: Ship logs to a separate logging account or project with S3 Object Lock, GCS bucket lock, or equivalent retention locks. Deny log deletion and trail modification with organization policies. Alert on events such as StopLogging, DeleteTrail, or sink deletion. Log generation and retention periods are covered by OGRL-LM-01.

log_reader_roles.label: Roles permitted to read audit logs
log_reader_roles.value: security and designated on-call engineering roles

log_store.label: Protected log storage location
log_store.value: a dedicated logging account or project separate from production workloads

mappings.summary: Protects audit information from unauthorized access, modification, and deletion, but protects logging tools only by alerting on configuration changes.
Blocks logged-system administrators from altering logs and alerts on logging configuration changes, but does not name the privileged subset allowed to manage logging.
Immutable storage and restricted access protect audit information from unauthorized access, modification, and deletion per AU-9(a).
Tampering alerts to defined recipients satisfy AU-9(b).
Restricting access to audit logs is a logical access protection over an information asset under CC6.1.
Trustworthy, tamper-resistant logs underpin the anomaly monitoring expected under CC7.2.

controls.name: Audit Log Review and Analysis
controls.summary: Periodically review high-risk audit logs, document findings, and escalate them.
controls.statement: Review and analyze {{ reviewed_log_sources }} {{ log_review_frequency }} for indications of {{ reviewed_activity }}, document each review with reviewer, date, and findings, report findings to {{ log_review_report_recipients }}, and increase review scope or frequency when incidents, threat intelligence, or significant system changes indicate elevated risk.
controls.objective: Identify inappropriate or unusual activity that automated alerting may not catch, and leave evidence that review occurred.
controls.guidance: Use saved SIEM queries or dashboards for each review so it is repeatable, and record the review as a ticket with the query output attached. Focus on privileged and administrative actions, break-glass usage, and changes to security tooling. Real-time automated alerting is covered by OGRL-LM-02.

log_review_report_recipients.label: Log review finding recipients
log_review_report_recipients.value: the security lead and affected system owners

reviewed_activity.label: Activity sought in log review
reviewed_activity.value: unauthorized privileged actions, anomalous authentication patterns, and disabled or modified security controls

reviewed_log_sources.label: Logs subject to periodic review
reviewed_log_sources.value: privileged and administrative activity logs, authentication logs, and security tooling configuration changes

mappings.summary: Log review for unauthorized privileged actions and anomalous authentication identifies unauthorized use, but does not define authorized use.
Defines the periodic audit record review, analysis, and reporting process; correlating it with other processes is covered by OGRL-LM-08.
Scheduled analysis of audit records for defined unusual activity satisfies AU-6(a).
Findings are reported to defined recipients per AU-6(b).
Review scope is adjusted when credible information indicates a change in risk, as AU-6(c) requires.
Documented recurring log reviews provide some ongoing evaluation evidence relevant to CC4.1.
Periodic analysis of audit logs for anomalies is a monitoring activity under CC7.2.
Documenting and escalating log review findings feeds the evaluation of security events under CC7.3.

controls.name: Processing Monitoring and Reconciliation
controls.summary: Monitor processing jobs for failures and reconcile inputs to outputs, correcting discrepancies promptly.
controls.statement: Monitor {{ monitored_processing_jobs }} for failures, delays, and incomplete runs, reconcile record counts or control totals between inputs and outputs {{ reconciliation_frequency }}, and route discrepancies to {{ processing_owner }} for investigation and correction within {{ discrepancy_resolution_sla }}.
controls.objective: Detect and correct incomplete or inaccurate processing before it affects customers or downstream systems.
controls.guidance: Emit job success, duration, and record-count metrics and alert on failures, missed schedules, and dead-letter queue depth. Automate reconciliation queries that compare source and destination counts or sums and open a ticket on mismatch. Evidence is the alert configuration plus a sample of reconciliation results and resolved discrepancy tickets.

monitored_processing_jobs.label: Processing monitored for completeness
monitored_processing_jobs.value: scheduled jobs, data pipelines, and queue consumers that process customer data

mappings.summary: Monitoring processing completion and reconciling volumes supports complete and accurate processing under PI1.3.

controls.name: Audit Logging Failure Alerting
controls.summary: Detect audit logging failures and alert designated personnel so logging is restored promptly.
controls.statement: Monitor the audit logging process for {{ logging_failure_types }}, automatically alert {{ logging_failure_alert_recipients }} within {{ logging_failure_alert_window }} of any such failure, and on each alert {{ logging_failure_actions }}.
controls.objective: Ensure that loss of audit logging is noticed and corrected quickly so gaps in the audit trail are minimized.
controls.guidance: Most failures are silent, so alert on the absence of expected data as well as on explicit errors: configure heartbeat or "no events received" detections per log source in the SIEM, alert on agent or forwarder health checks, and alert on cloud events such as CloudTrail StopLogging or DeleteTrail, Azure diagnostic setting deletion, or GCP sink deletion. Watch storage quota and ingestion license limits so logs are not dropped when capacity is reached. Small contractors using a managed SIEM or MSSP should confirm in the contract that the provider monitors source health and pages a named contact. Document the alert recipients and failure types in the system security plan. Evidence is the alert rule configuration, the recipient list, and a ticket from a real or test failure showing the alert and the follow-up actions. Protection of logs against tampering is covered by OGRL-LM-03.

logging_failure_actions.label: Actions taken on audit logging failure
logging_failure_actions.value: open a tracked ticket, restore log collection, and confirm whether events from the gap can be recovered from source systems or buffers

logging_failure_alert_recipients.label: Personnel or roles alerted on audit logging failure
logging_failure_alert_recipients.value: the security on-call team and the logging platform owner

logging_failure_alert_window.label: Time limit for alerting after a logging failure

logging_failure_types.label: Audit logging failure types that generate alerts
logging_failure_types.value: a log source that stops sending events, failure of a logging agent or forwarder, ingestion or parsing errors, log storage reaching capacity, and audit logging being disabled or reconfigured

mappings.summary: Defines the logging failure types and alert recipients and automatically alerts them on failure, meeting every 3.3.4 objective.
Alerting named personnel within a set time of an audit logging failure is AU-5(a).
The defined follow-up actions on each logging failure alert supply the AU-5(b) additional actions.

controls.name: Time Synchronization
controls.summary: Synchronize system clocks with an authoritative time source so audit record timestamps are accurate and comparable.
controls.statement: Configure every system that generates audit records to time-stamp audit records from its internal system clock, recording timestamps with a granularity of {{ timestamp_granularity }} in Coordinated Universal Time or with the UTC offset included; compare internal system clocks with {{ authoritative_time_source }} {{ time_comparison_frequency }}; and synchronize a clock to that source whenever its difference exceeds {{ max_clock_drift }}.
controls.objective: Ensure audit records from different systems carry accurate, consistent timestamps so events can be ordered and correlated during investigations.
controls.guidance: Cloud instances can use the provider time service (for example Amazon Time Sync Service, the Azure host time source, or Google internal NTP), which is traceable to UTC; on-premises systems and domain controllers should sync to a designated internal NTP hierarchy that in turn syncs to a trusted source such as NIST time servers. Run chrony, ntpd, or w32time with a polling interval that meets the comparison frequency and step or slew the clock when drift exceeds the threshold. For SaaS applications the provider generates timestamps; record that reliance in the system security plan and confirm that exported logs carry UTC timestamps. Evidence is the time configuration on a sample of systems, a drift report or chronyc tracking output, and sample audit records showing the timestamp format.

authoritative_time_source.label: Authoritative time source
authoritative_time_source.value: the designated cloud-provider time service or organizational NTP servers synchronized to a UTC-traceable source

mappings.summary: Clock-based audit timestamps compared and synchronized with a specified authoritative source meet every 3.3.7 objective.
Requires audit record timestamps to come from internal system clocks, as AU-8(a) does.
Sets timestamp granularity and requires UTC or an included UTC offset, matching AU-8(b).
Comparing internal clocks with the authoritative source at a defined frequency is SC-45(1)(a).
Synchronizing a clock when drift exceeds the defined threshold is SC-45(1)(b).

controls.name: Audit Record Correlation, Reduction, and Reporting
controls.summary: Correlate audit records across sources in a central platform that supports on-demand analysis and reporting, and tie review and response processes together.
controls.statement: Aggregate audit records from {{ correlated_log_sources }} into {{ log_analysis_platform }} that analyzes and correlates records across sources and provides on-demand filtering, search, and report generation without altering the original content or time ordering of stored audit records; route the results of automated alerting, periodic audit record review, and analysis into a single documented investigation and incident response workflow so indications of unlawful, unauthorized, suspicious, or unusual activity are correlated and handled consistently; and test {{ capability_test_frequency }} that on-demand queries and reports can be produced across all aggregated sources.
controls.objective: Enable analysts to see related activity across all log sources and to produce focused queries and reports on demand for investigation and response.
controls.guidance: A SIEM or cloud log analytics service (for example Microsoft Sentinel, Splunk, Elastic, Google Security Operations, or a managed SIEM from an MSSP) provides correlation, search, and reporting. Normalize fields such as user, host, source IP, and timestamp so a single query spans the identity provider, cloud control plane, endpoint, network, and application logs. Keep raw events read-only and run filters and reports against them rather than against edited copies. Write down how alert triage (OGRL-LM-02), periodic log review (OGRL-LM-04), and incident handling (OGRL-IR-02) hand off to one another so a finding in one becomes an investigation in another. Evidence is the list of connected sources, saved correlation searches and report templates, the written workflow, and the record of the most recent on-demand query and report test.

capability_test_frequency.label: Frequency of on-demand query and report testing

correlated_log_sources.label: Log sources aggregated and correlated
correlated_log_sources.value: all in-scope audit log sources, including identity provider, cloud control plane, endpoint, network, and application logs

log_analysis_platform.label: Log correlation and analysis platform
log_analysis_platform.value: a SIEM or centralized log analytics platform

mappings.summary: Correlates alerting, review, analysis, and response through one platform and workflow; the periodic review process itself is defined by OGRL-LM-04.
Provides audit record reduction and report generation for on- demand analysis and reporting, meeting both 3.3.6 objectives.
Aggregating and correlating audit records across all sources in one platform delivers the organization-wide view AU-6(3) requires.
On-demand filtering, search, and reporting over aggregated records supports review, analysis, reporting, and after-the-fact investigation per AU-7(a).
Requires reduction and reporting to leave original audit record content and time ordering unchanged, as AU-7(b) does.

controls.name: Privacy Notice
controls.summary: Publish a plain-language privacy notice at the point of collection and keep it current.
controls.statement: Publish a plain-language privacy notice at {{ notice_locations }} that is available before or at first collection of personal information and that states the purposes and legal basis for processing and includes {{ notice_contents }}; review the notice {{ notice_review_cadence }} and before any material change in processing, and inform affected individuals of material changes {{ notice_change_lead_time }}.
controls.objective: Ensure individuals are informed about how their personal information is processed before and while it is processed.
controls.guidance: Link the notice from sign-up flows, the website footer, and mobile app settings; keep a version history with effective dates. Have legal or the privacy lead confirm the notice still matches the PII inventory at each review.

notice_change_lead_time.label: Advance notice of material changes
notice_change_lead_time.value: at least 30 days before they take effect

notice_contents.label: Required privacy notice contents
notice_contents.value: data categories, sources, recipients, retention, individual rights, and contacts

notice_locations.label: Privacy notice locations
notice_locations.value: the public website and every point where personal information is collected

mappings.summary: A plain-language notice available at first collection stating purposes, legal basis, and defined contents covers PT-5.
Publishing and maintaining a privacy notice addresses the notice obligations in P1.1.

controls.name: Consent Management
controls.summary: Obtain, record, and honor withdrawal of consent wherever consent is the basis for processing personal information.
controls.statement: Where consent is the basis for processing, obtain informed, affirmative consent through {{ consent_mechanism }} before collecting personal information, obtain separate explicit consent before collecting {{ sensitive_pii_categories }}, record each consent with the individual, scope, timestamp, and notice version, and give effect to consent withdrawals within {{ consent_withdrawal_sla }}.
controls.objective: Ensure personal information processed on the basis of consent is backed by a valid, provable, and revocable consent.
controls.guidance: Use unchecked opt-in boxes or a consent management platform; store consent records in a system queryable by user ID. Withdrawal should be as easy as giving consent and must propagate to downstream processors such as marketing tools.

consent_mechanism.label: Consent collection mechanism
consent_mechanism.value: unbundled opt-in controls presented with a link to the privacy notice

sensitive_pii_categories.label: Sensitive personal information categories
sensitive_pii_categories.value: health, biometric, financial, precise location, or government ID data

mappings.summary: Pre-collection consent mechanisms satisfy PT-4; the control adds consent records and withdrawal handling.
Obtaining and recording consent addresses the choice and consent obligations in P2.1.
Separate explicit consent for sensitive categories addresses P3.2.

controls.name: Purpose Specification and Use Limitation
controls.summary: Document the purpose and legal authority for each PII processing activity and restrict use to those purposes.
controls.statement: Document the purposes and legal authority for each personal information processing activity, reflect those purposes in the privacy notice, restrict collection and use of personal information to the documented purposes, and require {{ purpose_change_review }} before personal information is processed for a new or changed purpose.
controls.objective: Prevent personal information from being used for purposes individuals were not told about or that lack a legal basis.
controls.guidance: Record purposes and legal basis per processing activity in the PII inventory (pr-05). Add a privacy checkbox to product and data-pipeline design reviews so new uses (analytics, ML training, marketing) trigger review before launch.

purpose_change_review.label: Review required for new or changed purposes
purpose_change_review.value: a documented privacy review approved by the privacy lead

mappings.summary: Documenting legal authority per activity and restricting processing to it addresses PT-2.
Documenting purposes, reflecting them in the notice, restricting use, and reviewing changes covers PT-3.
Limiting collection to documented purposes overlaps the collection objectives in P3.1.
Restricting use to documented purposes addresses the use limitation in P4.1.

controls.name: PII Minimization
controls.summary: Collect and retain only the personal information elements needed for each documented purpose.
controls.statement: Limit personal information collected and processed to {{ permitted_pii_elements }}, require {{ pii_element_approver }} to approve any new personal information element before collection begins, and review collection points and data stores {{ minimization_review_cadence }} to remove elements no longer needed.
controls.objective: Reduce privacy risk and breach impact by holding no more personal information than each purpose requires.
controls.guidance: Enforce minimization in form and API schemas, and use data discovery or schema diffs to spot unapproved fields. Prefer pseudonymized or aggregated data for analytics and testing.

permitted_pii_elements.label: Permitted personal information elements
permitted_pii_elements.value: the elements approved for each processing activity in the PII inventory

pii_element_approver.label: Approver for new personal information elements

mappings.summary: Limiting processing to approved PII elements satisfies SI-12(1).
Collecting only necessary PII elements addresses P3.1.
Minimizing processed elements supports limiting use of personal information under P4.1.

controls.name: PII Inventory and Processing Records
controls.summary: Maintain an inventory of systems, vendors, and processing activities that handle personal information.
controls.statement: Maintain an inventory of systems, applications, vendors, and projects that process personal information, recording for each the personal information categories, data subjects, purposes, legal basis, storage locations, recipients, and retention period; update it when processing changes and review it in full {{ pii_inventory_review_cadence }}.
controls.objective: Provide an accurate record of where personal information lives and how it flows, enabling notice, rights requests, and risk management.
controls.guidance: A spreadsheet or data-map tool is sufficient; seed it from the system and vendor inventories and data-discovery scans. Make updates part of the change and vendor-onboarding workflows.

mappings.summary: A maintained and periodically reviewed inventory of PII-processing systems satisfies PM-5(1).
Recording purposes and recipients per activity enables but does not enforce use limitation under P4.1.
The inventory supplies the data needed to tell individuals what is held and shared, supporting P6.7.

controls.name: Data Subject Access Requests
controls.summary: Give individuals a way to request and receive the personal information held about them, within a defined timeline.
controls.statement: Provide {{ access_request_channels }} through which individuals can request access to their personal information, verify the requester's identity using {{ requester_verification_method }}, provide {{ access_request_elements }} within {{ access_request_sla }}, and log each request, its outcome, and the reason for any denial.
controls.objective: Enable individuals to learn what personal information the organization holds about them in a timely and secure manner.
controls.guidance: Track requests in a ticketing queue with due dates; use the PII inventory (pr-05) to locate data across systems and processors. Avoid over-collecting identity documents for verification; matching account login or a verified email is usually enough.

access_request_channels.label: Access request channels
access_request_channels.value: a web form and a published privacy email address

access_request_elements.label: Personal information disclosed in response
access_request_elements.value: a copy of their personal information and its categories, sources, and recipients

requester_verification_method.label: Requester identity verification method
requester_verification_method.value: account authentication or confirmation via the email address on file

mappings.summary: Request channels and defined disclosed elements implement individual access under AC-3(14).
Verified, timely access-request fulfillment addresses individual access under P5.1.

controls.name: Data Subject Correction Requests
controls.summary: Correct or delete personal information on verified request and propagate the change to recipients.
controls.statement: Accept requests from individuals or their authorized representatives to correct or delete their personal information, verify the requester's identity, complete the correction or deletion within {{ correction_request_sla }} across all systems in the PII inventory, notify third parties that received the information, and record the reason when a request is denied and communicate it to the requester.
controls.objective: Ensure individuals can have inaccurate or unwanted personal information fixed or removed and that changes reach downstream recipients.
controls.guidance: Reuse the access-request intake and ticket queue (pr-06). Automate deletion through account-deletion workflows where possible and keep evidence of processor notifications. Legal holds and retention obligations are valid denial reasons when documented.

mappings.summary: Correcting or deleting PII on verified request satisfies SI-18(4).
Correction handling with recipient notification and denial reasons addresses P5.2.

controls.name: Third-Party Disclosure Authorization
controls.summary: Approve each new third-party recipient of personal information against the permitted uses of that information.
controls.statement: Before disclosing personal information to a new third party or for a new purpose in {{ disclosure_circumstances }}, require {{ disclosure_approver }} to confirm that the disclosure is consistent with the privacy notice and any consent obtained and that a written agreement binds the recipient to equivalent privacy and confidentiality obligations.
controls.objective: Ensure personal information is shared only with recipients and for uses that individuals were informed of and that contracts restrict.
controls.guidance: Embed the privacy check in vendor onboarding and in data-sharing requests; maintain the approved recipient list as the public subprocessor list where applicable. A data processing agreement with standard privacy terms meets the written-agreement requirement.

disclosure_circumstances.label: Disclosure circumstances requiring authorization
disclosure_circumstances.value: any sharing of personal information with a party outside the organization

mappings.summary: Approval of PII recipients against permitted uses overlaps the sharing-partner check in AC-21(a); automated aids in AC-21(b) are not covered.
Authorizing third-party disclosures against notice, consent, and contract addresses P6.1.

controls.name: Accounting of Disclosures
controls.summary: Record disclosures of personal information to third parties and make the record available to affected individuals on request.
controls.statement: Record each disclosure of personal information to a third party with the date, nature and purpose of the disclosure, and the recipient's name and contact information, retain each record for {{ disclosure_record_retention }}, and provide individuals with the record of disclosures of their personal information within {{ disclosure_accounting_sla }} of request.
controls.objective: Maintain a reliable history of who received personal information and why, supporting individual rights and investigations.
controls.guidance: Routine sharing with contracted processors can be recorded at category level via the subprocessor list and PII inventory; ad hoc disclosures (law enforcement requests, data transfers to partners, unauthorized disclosures found during incidents) should be logged individually in a ticket or register.

disclosure_record_retention.label: Disclosure record retention period
disclosure_record_retention.value: the longer of the life of the information or five years after disclosure

mappings.summary: Recording disclosure details, retaining them, and providing them on request covers PM-21.
Logging disclosures with date, purpose, and recipient addresses P6.2.
Providing individuals their disclosure record covers the disclosure portion of P6.7.

controls.name: PII Data Quality
controls.summary: Periodically check personal information for accuracy and completeness and fix or remove bad data.
controls.statement: Validate personal information at collection, check the accuracy, completeness, relevance, and timeliness of stored personal information {{ pii_quality_check_cadence }}, and correct or delete inaccurate or outdated personal information within {{ pii_quality_remediation_sla }} of detection.
controls.objective: Ensure decisions and communications that rely on personal information are based on accurate and current data.
controls.guidance: Input validation, self-service profile editing, and bounce or undeliverable handling cover most needs. Periodic checks can be automated data-quality queries or stale-record reports reviewed by the data owner.

mappings.summary: Periodic accuracy, completeness, relevance, and timeliness checks satisfy SI-18(a).
Correcting or deleting inaccurate or outdated PII satisfies SI-18(b).
Validating and correcting personal information addresses data quality under P7.1.

controls.name: Privacy Inquiry and Complaint Management
controls.summary: Receive, track, and respond to privacy inquiries and complaints within defined timelines under an accountable privacy lead.
controls.statement: Designate {{ privacy_lead_role }} as accountable for privacy inquiries and complaints, publish {{ complaint_channels }} together with the information needed to file a complaint, track each inquiry or complaint to closure, acknowledge it within {{ complaint_acknowledgement_sla }}, respond within {{ complaint_response_sla }}, and resolve or escalate it within {{ complaint_resolution_sla }}.
controls.objective: Ensure individuals' privacy concerns are heard, addressed in a timely way, and used to improve privacy practices.
controls.guidance: A shared privacy mailbox feeding a ticket queue with SLA timers is usually enough. Report complaint volume and themes to leadership periodically and feed recurring issues into the privacy risk assessment.

complaint_channels.label: Privacy complaint channels
complaint_channels.value: a privacy email address and web form linked from the privacy notice

mappings.summary: Designating an accountable privacy lead for complaints is a narrow part of the privacy leadership role in PM-19.
Published channels, filing information, tracking, and acknowledgement, response, and resolution timelines cover PM-26.
Tracked intake and timely response to privacy inquiries and complaints addresses P8.1.

controls.name: Physical Access Authorization and Review
controls.summary: Keep an approved list of people allowed into controlled facilities, review it regularly, and remove access promptly when it is no longer needed.
controls.statement: Maintain a list of individuals authorized to enter {{ controlled_facilities }}, issue badges, keys, or other access credentials only after approval by {{ access_approver }}, review the list {{ access_review_cadence }}, and remove an individual's physical access within {{ access_removal_sla }} of termination or when access is no longer required.
controls.objective: Ensure only currently authorized individuals hold credentials that grant entry to facilities housing personnel or system components.
controls.guidance: Use the badge or door-access system as the source of truth and reconcile it against the HR roster during each review; tie offboarding tickets to badge deactivation so removal evidence is automatic. Coworking or shared offices can rely on the landlord's badge system if the organization can obtain the list of its credential holders. Where production runs on a cloud provider, data-center physical controls are inherited from the provider and validated by reviewing its SOC 2 report; offices and any organization-operated server, network, or storage rooms remain in scope.

access_approver.label: Physical access approval authority
access_approver.value: the facilities owner or the requester's manager

controlled_facilities.label: Controlled facilities
controlled_facilities.value: company offices and any organization-operated server, network, or storage rooms

mappings.summary: Identifies and approves the individuals allowed physical access and removes access promptly; enforcement at entry points is provided by OGRL-PS-02.
Approved access list, credential issuance, periodic review, and timely removal cover all of PE-2.
Authorizing and reviewing who may enter facilities is one part of restricting physical access under CC6.4.

controls.name: Physical Access Control
controls.summary: Enforce authorized entry at every facility entry point and keep keys, badges, and combinations under inventory and control.
controls.statement: Enforce physical access authorizations at every entry and exit point of {{ controlled_facilities }} using {{ entry_control_mechanism }}, retain electronic entry logs for {{ entry_log_retention }}, secure unissued keys, badges, and combinations, inventory physical access devices {{ access_device_inventory_cadence }}, and change combinations or rekey locks when a key or code is lost or compromised or its holder leaves.
controls.objective: Prevent unauthorized individuals from entering facilities that house personnel or system components, and keep a record of who entered.
controls.guidance: Badge readers that log each entry satisfy both enforcement and logging; areas that rely on physical keys need a key register. Inventory issued badges against ps-01's authorized list to catch orphaned credentials. Where production runs on a cloud provider, data-center physical controls are inherited from the provider and validated by reviewing its SOC 2 report; offices and any organization-operated server, network, or storage rooms remain in scope.

controlled_facilities.label: Controlled facilities
controlled_facilities.value: company offices and any organization-operated server, network, or storage rooms

entry_control_mechanism.label: Entry control mechanism
entry_control_mechanism.value: electronic badge readers or keyed locks

mappings.summary: Enforces physical access authorizations at every facility entry point; together with the authorized-individual list in OGRL-PS-01 this limits physical access to authorized individuals.
Enforced entry control at controlled facilities protects the physical facility; monitoring and support-infrastructure protection come from other controls.
Retains electronic entry logs at controlled facilities, but areas secured only by keyed locks produce no physical access log.
Physical access devices are secured, inventoried, and rekeyed or changed on loss or holder departure, and the control also enforces entry and logging.
Badge or lock enforcement at every entry and exit point satisfies PE-3(a).
Retained electronic entry logs at controlled entry points satisfy PE-3(b).
Securing unissued keys, badges, and combinations satisfies PE-3(e).
Periodic inventory of physical access devices satisfies PE-3(f).
Event-triggered rekeying covers PE-3(g) except the periodic change cadence.
Enforced entry at facility access points is a core piece of physical access restriction under CC6.4.

controls.name: Visitor Access Records
controls.summary: Log every visitor, escort them in non-public areas, and review the visitor log for anomalies.
controls.statement: Record each visitor to {{ controlled_facilities }} with name, organization, host, and times of arrival and departure, escort visitors in non-public areas, retain visitor records for {{ visitor_record_retention }}, review the records {{ visitor_review_cadence }}, and report anomalies to {{ visitor_anomaly_recipient }}.
controls.objective: Maintain accountability for non-workforce individuals who enter facilities and detect unusual visitor activity.
controls.guidance: A tablet-based visitor management system or front-desk sign-in sheet both work; capture host and badge-return evidence. Anomalies include unescorted visitors, missing sign-outs, and unreturned visitor badges. In shared buildings, building-reception logs may be used if the organization can retrieve entries for its own visitors. Where production runs on a cloud provider, data-center physical controls are inherited from the provider and validated by reviewing its SOC 2 report; offices and any organization-operated server, network, or storage rooms remain in scope.

controlled_facilities.label: Controlled facilities
controlled_facilities.value: company offices and any organization-operated server, network, or storage rooms

mappings.summary: Visitors are escorted in non-public areas and their activity is recorded and reviewed for anomalies.
Visitor records with arrival and departure times form the visitor portion of the physical access audit log.
Escorting visitors in non-public areas addresses PE-3(d) without broader visitor activity controls.
Visitor logging, retention, periodic review, and anomaly reporting cover PE-8.
Visitor logging and escort contribute to restricting physical access under CC6.4.

controls.name: Physical Access Monitoring
controls.summary: Monitor facility entry points and review physical access logs to detect and escalate physical security incidents.
controls.statement: Monitor entry points of {{ controlled_facilities }} using {{ physical_monitoring_mechanisms }}, review physical access logs {{ access_log_review_cadence }} and upon {{ access_log_review_triggers }}, and escalate suspected physical security incidents to the incident response process.
controls.objective: Detect unauthorized or suspicious physical access in time to respond and feed findings into incident response.
controls.guidance: Configure badge-system alerts for forced or held-open doors and after-hours entry, and keep camera footage long enough to support investigations. Record each review (date, reviewer, exceptions) as evidence. Where production runs on a cloud provider, data-center physical controls are inherited from the provider and validated by reviewing its SOC 2 report; offices and any organization-operated server, network, or storage rooms remain in scope.

access_log_review_triggers.label: Events triggering an ad hoc log review
access_log_review_triggers.value: door alarms, forced-entry alerts, or reported physical security incidents

controlled_facilities.label: Controlled facilities
controlled_facilities.value: company offices and any organization-operated server, network, or storage rooms

physical_monitoring_mechanisms.label: Physical monitoring mechanisms
physical_monitoring_mechanisms.value: video surveillance and door alarms or badge-system alerts

mappings.summary: Monitors facility entry points and escalates incidents, covering facility monitoring but not protection of the facility or its support infrastructure.
Entry-point monitoring, scheduled and triggered log reviews, and incident escalation cover PE-6.
Monitoring physical entry supports enforcement of facility access restrictions under CC6.4.
Physical access monitoring is one source of anomaly detection relevant to CC7.2, which is broader.

controls.name: Environmental Safeguards
controls.summary: Protect organization-operated equipment rooms with environmental monitoring, backup power, fire protection, and water-damage protection.
controls.statement: In each organization-operated facility that houses in-scope system components, maintain {{ environmental_factors }} within {{ environmental_ranges }} and monitor them {{ environmental_monitoring_cadence }} with alerting; provide an uninterruptible power supply sufficient to allow {{ ups_capability }}; employ fire detection and suppression systems with an independent power source; and keep master water shutoff or isolation valves accessible, working, and known to facilities personnel.
controls.objective: Prevent loss of availability or equipment damage from environmental hazards in facilities the organization operates.
controls.guidance: Applies only to server rooms, network closets, or on-premises data centers run by the organization. For cloud-hosted production, these safeguards are inherited from the provider and validated through its SOC 2 report; document the inheritance and review the report each year. Office spaces with only laptops and a network switch typically need only UPS for network gear and landlord-provided fire protection.

environmental_ranges.label: Acceptable environmental ranges
environmental_ranges.value: the equipment manufacturer's recommended operating ranges

ups_capability.label: Uninterruptible power supply capability
ups_capability.value: an orderly shutdown of in-scope systems

mappings.summary: Protects and monitors environmental and power support infrastructure in organization-operated facilities, but not facility entry protection or monitoring.
Providing a UPS sized for the defined capability satisfies PE-11.
Fire detection and suppression with independent power satisfies PE-13.
Maintaining and monitoring environmental conditions within defined ranges satisfies PE-14.
Accessible, working, known master water shutoff valves satisfy PE-15.
Environmental protections for organization-operated facilities are one part of A1.2.

controls.name: Equipment Delivery and Removal
controls.summary: Authorize and record system components entering or leaving organization facilities.
controls.statement: Authorize and record {{ controlled_component_types }} entering and leaving {{ controlled_facilities }}, require approval from {{ removal_approver }} before such components are removed, and record the asset identifier, date, responsible person, and purpose of each movement in the asset inventory.
controls.objective: Ensure that system components cannot enter or leave organization facilities without authorization and a traceable record.
controls.guidance: Track movements in the asset management system or ticketing tool; laptops assigned to employees for routine use need not be logged at each trip, but receipt, reassignment, repair shipment, and disposal should be. Pair with media sanitization controls for components leaving for repair or disposal. Where production runs on a cloud provider, data-center physical controls are inherited from the provider and validated by reviewing its SOC 2 report; offices and any organization-operated server, network, or storage rooms remain in scope.

controlled_component_types.label: Component types subject to movement control
controlled_component_types.value: servers, network devices, storage media, and workforce endpoints

controlled_facilities.label: Controlled facilities
controlled_facilities.value: company offices and any organization-operated server, network, or storage rooms

mappings.summary: Authorizing and recording component movements in and out of facilities covers PE-16.
Controlling equipment entering and leaving facilities contributes to physical protection under CC6.4.
Approved, recorded removal of components supports control over assets leaving the organization under CC6.5.

controls.name: Facility and Infrastructure Maintenance
controls.summary: Schedule, approve, record, and verify maintenance on supporting infrastructure and system components in organization facilities.
controls.statement: Schedule maintenance of in-scope system components and supporting facility infrastructure in organization-operated facilities according to manufacturer or vendor specifications, require approval by {{ maintenance_approver }} for maintenance activities and for removing components off-site for service, verify affected safeguards function after maintenance, record {{ maintenance_record_contents }}, and review maintenance records {{ maintenance_review_cadence }}.
controls.objective: Keep supporting infrastructure reliable and ensure maintenance does not introduce unauthorized changes or degrade safeguards.
controls.guidance: Supporting infrastructure includes UPS units, HVAC, fire suppression, generators, and on-premises network or server hardware. Keep vendor service reports with the maintenance record. For cloud-hosted production, data-center maintenance is inherited from the provider and validated through its SOC 2 report; this control then covers only office or organization-operated equipment rooms.

maintenance_record_contents.label: Required maintenance record contents
maintenance_record_contents.value: date, component, maintenance performed, performer, and approver

mappings.summary: Scheduling maintenance to vendor specifications and reviewing records satisfies MA-2(a).
Approval of maintenance activities covers MA-2(b) except explicit monitoring of each activity.
Required approval before off-site removal for service satisfies MA-2(c).
Post-maintenance verification of affected safeguards satisfies MA-2(e).
Defined maintenance record contents satisfy MA-2(f).
Maintaining supporting infrastructure contributes to the availability protections in A1.2.

controls.name: Removable Media and Portable Storage Control
controls.summary: Block removable media by default, allow only owned and approved organization devices, and tightly limit their use on external systems.
controls.statement: Block the use of {{ removable_media_types }} on {{ in_scope_endpoints }} by default using {{ media_enforcement_mechanism }}, allowing only organization-issued devices that are recorded in the asset inventory with an identifiable owner and approved on a documented allow-list; prohibit the use of any portable storage device that has no identifiable owner; permit organization-controlled portable storage devices containing CUI to be used on external systems only for documented, approved uses that meet {{ external_system_media_restrictions }}; and review the allow-list and approved external-system uses {{ media_exception_review_cadence }}.
controls.objective: Prevent CUI from leaving, or malicious content from entering, organizational systems through uncontrolled removable media and portable storage devices.
controls.guidance: Use the MDM or EDR device-control feature (for example Microsoft Intune device control, Defender for Endpoint, Jamf, or CrowdStrike USB device control) to block mass-storage devices by default and allow only approved devices by serial number or hardware ID, so the allow-list doubles as the owner record. Record each issued device in the asset inventory with its owner; found, gifted, or conference-giveaway devices have no identifiable owner and stay blocked. External systems include customer, prime-contractor, and government systems, personal devices, and hotel or kiosk computers; most small contractors can simply prohibit CUI on portable storage outside the organization and exchange files through an approved CUI-capable file transfer service instead. Remote workers are covered because the policy is enforced on the managed endpoint rather than the network. Retain the device-control policy export, the allow-list, and blocked-device events as evidence.

external_system_media_restrictions.label: Restrictions on organization-controlled portable storage used on external systems
external_system_media_restrictions.value: prior written approval by the security owner recording the device, the CUI involved, the external system, and the business purpose; FIPS-validated encryption of the device; and connection only to the external system named in the approval

in_scope_endpoints.label: Systems and system components on which removable media use is controlled
in_scope_endpoints.value: all organization-managed workstations, laptops, and servers that process, store, or transmit CUI

media_enforcement_mechanism.label: Technical mechanism enforcing removable media restrictions
media_enforcement_mechanism.value: centrally managed endpoint device-control policies (MDM or EDR) that block read and write access to unapproved mass-storage devices

media_exception_review_cadence.label: Removable media allow-list and exception review frequency

removable_media_types.label: Types of removable media and portable storage devices controlled
removable_media_types.value: USB flash drives, external hard and solid-state drives, memory cards, writable optical discs, and mobile devices operating in mass-storage mode

mappings.summary: Approved external-system uses are documented, the restrictions on them are defined, and use is limited to those approvals, meeting every 3.1.21 objective.
Technically enforced default-deny device control with an approved allow-list controls removable media on system components.
Blocking ownerless portable storage satisfies 3.8.8, and the control goes further by allowing only inventoried organization-issued devices.
Organization-controlled portable storage may be used on external systems only for approved uses meeting defined restrictions, which is AC-20(2).
Default-deny device control on in-scope endpoints, with an owned and approved allow-list, restricts removable media use as MP-7(a) requires.
The control explicitly prohibits portable storage devices with no identifiable owner, matching MP-7(b).

controls.name: Physical Media Storage and Access
controls.summary: Keep CUI media in an authorized person's custody or locked storage and restrict access to it to authorized users.
controls.statement: Physically control {{ cui_media_types }} so that it remains in the direct custody of an authorized user while in use and is stored in {{ secure_storage_containers }} within {{ media_controlled_areas }} whenever it is not in use; restrict access to that media and to the keys or combinations for its storage to {{ media_authorized_roles }}; maintain these protections until the media is sanitized or destroyed; and review the record of individuals with access to CUI media storage {{ media_access_review_cadence }}.
controls.objective: Ensure paper and digital media containing CUI is always either in the custody of an authorized user or locked in secure storage, so that only authorized individuals can access the CUI it holds.
controls.guidance: Most small contractors hold little physical CUI media; inventory what exists (printouts, drawings, approved USB drives, backup drives) and minimize it. A lockable cabinet or safe in a room with controlled entry (OGRL-PS-02) is usually sufficient; record who holds keys or combinations and treat that list as the access list for this control. Apply a clean-desk rule so CUI media is never left unattended outside storage, including printer output trays. Remote workers who are approved to hold CUI media at home (OGRL-PS-12) need a locking drawer or container. Laptops and phones that store CUI are digital media too: keep them in the holder's custody or locked away, and rely on FIPS-validated full-disk encryption (OGRL-CR-06) as the logical safeguard. Cloud-hosted CUI is protected through logical access controls and the provider's inherited physical controls; this control covers media the organization physically holds.

cui_media_types.label: Types of paper and digital media containing CUI to protect
cui_media_types.value: paper documents and printouts, removable and portable digital media, external drives, backup media, and portable computing devices that store CUI

media_access_review_cadence.label: Frequency of reviewing who can access CUI media storage

media_authorized_roles.label: Personnel authorized to access CUI media
media_authorized_roles.value: workforce members authorized for the CUI contained on the media and designated media custodians

media_controlled_areas.label: Controlled areas in which CUI media is stored
media_controlled_areas.value: organization-controlled offices and equipment rooms with enforced entry control, and alternate work sites approved for CUI handling

secure_storage_containers.label: Secure storage for CUI media not in use
secure_storage_containers.value: locked cabinets, drawers, safes, or locked rooms

mappings.summary: Both paper and digital CUI media are physically controlled while in use and securely stored when not, covering all four 3.8.1 objectives.
Restricting CUI media and its storage keys to authorized personnel, with periodic review, limits access to CUI on media to authorized users.
Access to defined CUI media types and their storage is restricted to defined authorized personnel, as MP-2 requires.
Defined CUI media is kept in authorized custody or locked storage within defined controlled areas, meeting MP-4(a).
Protections remain in force until the media is sanitized or destroyed; the sanitization technique itself is governed by OGRL-CR-04.

controls.name: CUI Media Marking
controls.summary: Mark CUI media with CUI banners and distribution limitations per DoD CUI rules and spot-check that marking is applied.
controls.statement: Mark {{ cui_marking_media_types }} with the CUI banner marking, the applicable CUI category or designation indicator, and any limited dissemination control or distribution statement specified by the contract or originating agency, in accordance with {{ cui_marking_authority }}; exempt only {{ marking_exempt_media }} from marking, and only while it remains within {{ marking_exempt_areas }}; and sample CUI media for correct marking {{ marking_review_cadence }}, correcting deficiencies found.
controls.objective: Ensure every recipient of media containing CUI can recognize that it holds CUI and knows the dissemination limits that apply.
controls.guidance: Follow the DoD CUI Registry and DoDI 5200.48 marking guide: a "CUI" or "CONTROLLED" banner at the top and bottom of each page, a CUI designation indicator block on the first page, portion marking where used, and any limited dissemination control (for example NOFORN or FEDCON) or DoD distribution statement (B through F for controlled technical information) carried over from the source material or contract (DD Form 254 or contract clauses). Label removable media and its case with the CUI banner and distribution limitation; where a label cannot fit, mark the container or envelope. Provide document templates and email or DLP labels with pre-filled CUI banners so remote workers mark consistently, and include marking in CUI handling training. Sample recently created CUI documents and media during each review and correct any that are unmarked or mismarked.

cui_marking_authority.label: Authoritative CUI marking requirements
cui_marking_authority.value: 32 CFR Part 2002, the DoD CUI Registry, and DoDI 5200.48 banner, designation indicator, and portion marking requirements

cui_marking_media_types.label: Media that must carry CUI markings
cui_marking_media_types.value: paper documents and printouts, removable and portable digital media and their containers, and electronic documents containing CUI

marking_exempt_areas.label: Controlled areas within which exempt media may remain unmarked
marking_exempt_areas.value: organization-controlled areas with enforced entry control

marking_exempt_media.label: Media types exempt from marking while in controlled areas
marking_exempt_media.value: non-removable internal storage drives of organization-managed system components

marking_review_cadence.label: Frequency of sampling CUI media for marking compliance

mappings.summary: Media containing CUI is marked with CUI markings and distribution limitations per the DoD CUI rules, meeting both 3.8.4 objectives.
CUI media carries banner, category, and dissemination or distribution markings, satisfying MP-3(a).
Marking exemptions are limited to defined media types while they remain in defined controlled areas, as MP-3(b) allows.

controls.name: Media Transport Protection
controls.summary: Encrypt or physically safeguard CUI media leaving controlled areas, limit who carries it, and log each shipment through to receipt.
controls.statement: Transport {{ transport_media_types }} outside of controlled areas only by {{ authorized_couriers }} and protect it using {{ transport_protection_controls }}; protect the confidentiality of CUI on digital media during transport using {{ transport_encryption_mechanism }}, or, where encryption is not feasible, using {{ alternative_physical_safeguards }}; record each transport in a media transport log with the media identifier, sender, recipient, courier, protection applied, and dates of dispatch and confirmed receipt; and reconcile open log entries {{ transport_log_reconciliation_cadence }}, investigating any media not confirmed as received.
controls.objective: Keep CUI on media protected from disclosure and accounted for from the moment it leaves a controlled area until it is received or returned.
controls.guidance: The simplest compliant approach is to avoid physical transport and move CUI through an approved encrypted file transfer service; keep this control for the cases that remain (shipping drives to a customer, carrying drawings to a site visit, couriering backup media). Use hardware-encrypted USB drives with a FIPS 140-2 or 140-3 certificate, or FIPS-validated encrypted archives, and send the passphrase or key through a separate channel. A shared spreadsheet or ticket queue works as the transport log; reconcile entries without a confirmed receipt and treat missing media as a security incident. Laptops carried by travelling or remote workers are media in transport: FIPS-validated full-disk encryption (OGRL-CR-06) satisfies the cryptographic requirement, and routine carriage by the assigned owner does not need a log entry. Paper CUI relies on the physical safeguards and logging alone.

alternative_physical_safeguards.label: Alternative physical safeguards used when digital media cannot be encrypted
alternative_physical_safeguards.value: a locked container kept in the continuous personal custody of an authorized courier, with the exception approved in advance by the security owner

authorized_couriers.label: Personnel and carriers authorized to transport CUI media
authorized_couriers.value: workforce members authorized for the CUI being transported, or commercial carriers providing tracking and signature confirmation

transport_encryption_mechanism.label: Cryptographic protection for CUI on digital media in transport
transport_encryption_mechanism.value: FIPS 140-2 or FIPS 140-3 validated encryption of the device or files, with keys or passphrases delivered separately from the media

transport_log_reconciliation_cadence.label: Frequency of reconciling open media transport log entries

transport_media_types.label: Types of media containing CUI controlled during transport
transport_media_types.value: paper documents and removable or portable digital media containing CUI

transport_protection_controls.label: Controls protecting media during transport
transport_protection_controls.value: sealed, opaque, tamper-evident packaging addressed to a named recipient, with the media kept in the courier's custody or tracked carrier chain of custody until delivery

mappings.summary: Restricting couriers, sealing packaging, and logging each shipment to receipt control access to and maintain accountability for CUI media in transport.
CUI on digital media is encrypted with FIPS-validated cryptography during transport, or protected by approved alternative physical safeguards, as 3.8.6 permits.
Defined CUI media leaving controlled areas is protected with defined packaging and custody controls, as MP-5(a) requires.
A transport log with confirmed receipt and periodic reconciliation maintains accountability for media in transit.
Every transport is documented in the media transport log, satisfying MP-5(c).
Only authorized workforce members or approved tracked carriers may transport CUI media, satisfying MP-5(d).
Encrypting CUI on digital media in transport applies SC-28(1) only to transported media; at-rest encryption elsewhere is handled by other controls.

controls.name: Alternate Work Site Safeguards
controls.summary: Define where remote work with CUI is allowed and which safeguards apply there, and verify that remote workers follow them.
controls.statement: Permit CUI to be accessed or handled outside organization-controlled facilities only at {{ approved_alternate_work_sites }}, as documented in the alternate work site standard; require at those sites that users {{ alternate_site_safeguards }}; require each user to acknowledge the safeguards before alternate-site CUI access is granted; provide {{ incident_reporting_channel }} for reporting suspected incidents; and assess compliance with the safeguards {{ alternate_site_assessment_cadence }} using {{ alternate_site_assessment_method }}.
controls.objective: Ensure CUI handled outside organization-controlled facilities receives defined safeguards that are actually followed.
controls.guidance: Publish a short remote-work or telework security standard that lists approved site types and the required safeguards, and have each remote worker acknowledge it in the HR or training system before CUI access is granted. Enforce the technical safeguards through MDM compliance policies and conditional access so that only compliant, managed devices reach CUI systems (pair with OGRL-CR-06 for FIPS-validated encryption and the remote-access controls in the AC family). For physical safeguards that cannot be enforced technically, an annual self-assessment questionnaire with photos of the workspace and locking storage, plus spot checks, gives the assessor evidence of enforcement. Coworking spaces, hotels, and customer sites are alternate work sites too; decide explicitly whether they are approved for CUI and say so in the standard.

alternate_site_assessment_cadence.label: Frequency of assessing safeguards at alternate work sites

alternate_site_assessment_method.label: Method for assessing alternate work site safeguards
alternate_site_assessment_method.value: remote worker self-assessment attestations, review of endpoint compliance reports, and follow-up of any exceptions

alternate_site_safeguards.label: Safeguards required at alternate work sites
alternate_site_safeguards.value: access CUI only from organization-managed, encrypted devices through the organization's approved remote access service; lock screens and secure devices and any CUI media in a locked room or container when unattended; position screens and hold conversations so household members and the public cannot see or hear CUI; and print CUI only when authorized, storing and destroying printouts per media protection controls

approved_alternate_work_sites.label: Alternate work sites approved for handling CUI
approved_alternate_work_sites.value: employees' private home offices and other sites approved in writing by the security owner; public spaces such as cafes, airports, and coworking common areas are not approved

incident_reporting_channel.label: Means for remote workers to report security incidents
incident_reporting_channel.value: the security team's documented incident reporting channel, available by phone and email

mappings.summary: Safeguards for CUI at alternate work sites are defined, acknowledged by users, and enforced and assessed, meeting both 3.10.6 objectives.
Approved alternate work sites for CUI are defined and documented in the alternate work site standard.
Defined safeguards are required of every user working with CUI at alternate work sites.
Compliance with alternate work site safeguards is assessed on a defined cadence using a defined method.
Remote workers are given a documented channel to report suspected incidents to security personnel.

controls.name: Risk Management Strategy
controls.summary: Maintain an approved risk management methodology that defines risk appetite, scoring, acceptance authority, and treatment options.
controls.statement: Maintain a documented risk management methodology that defines risk appetite and tolerance thresholds, likelihood and impact scoring criteria, the treatment options available, and that risk acceptance requires approval by {{ risk_acceptance_authority }}. The methodology is approved by {{ strategy_approver }} and reviewed and updated {{ strategy_review_frequency }} or when significant organizational changes occur.
controls.objective: Risks are identified, rated, and treated consistently against criteria that leadership has approved.
controls.guidance: A two-page method is enough for a startup: a 5x5 likelihood and impact matrix with defined levels, a tolerance line above which risks must be treated, and named acceptance authority by risk level. The risk assessment (OGRL-RM-02) and treatment tracking (OGRL-RM-04) apply this method.

risk_acceptance_authority.label: Risk acceptance authority
risk_acceptance_authority.value: the CEO for high risks and the security leader for others

mappings.summary: The approved methodology is the organization's strategy for managing security risk.
Periodic and change-driven review of the methodology meets the strategy review requirement.
Defined tolerance and scoring criteria enable risks to objectives to be identified and assessed.
The methodology sets how risks are analyzed and how responses are determined; the assessment itself is a separate control.
Defined treatment options, including transfer, frame how disruption risks are mitigated.

controls.name: Periodic Risk Assessment
controls.summary: Identify and rate threats and vulnerabilities to in-scope systems on a fixed cadence and record the results in the risk register.
controls.statement: Perform a risk assessment of in-scope systems {{ risk_assessment_frequency }} that identifies threats and vulnerabilities, including those arising from vendors and subservice organizations, and rates the likelihood and impact of each risk using the approved methodology. Record results in {{ risk_register }} and communicate them to {{ results_audience }}.
controls.objective: Leadership has a current, rated view of the risks to in-scope systems and the data they handle.
controls.guidance: Run a structured workshop with engineering, product, and operations; seed it with incidents, vulnerability trends, vendor reviews, and audit findings from the period. Each register entry needs a description, affected assets, inherent rating, existing controls, residual rating, and owner. Evidence: the dated register snapshot and its sign-off.

results_audience.label: Recipients of risk assessment results
results_audience.value: executive leadership and the board or its designated committee

mappings.summary: A risk assessment at a defined frequency that rates likelihood and impact meets 3.11.1.
The assessment identifies threats to and vulnerabilities in the system.
Likelihood and impact ratings determine the likelihood and magnitude of harm.
Results are documented in the risk register.
Results are communicated to named recipients.
Covers the periodic update; change-driven updates are handled by significant change risk evaluation.
The assessment is the mechanism through which risks to stated objectives are identified.
Identifies and rates risks to the system, including vendor risks; deciding how to respond is handled by risk treatment.

controls.name: Fraud Risk Assessment
controls.summary: Assess the potential for fraud, including management override, as part of risk assessment and document the controls that address it.
controls.statement: Assess fraud risk {{ fraud_assessment_frequency }}, considering motive, opportunity, and rationalization for the workforce and third parties, the potential for management override of controls, and fraud scenarios relevant to the system such as misuse of privileged access or manipulation of customer or billing data. Document each scenario with its rating and mitigating controls, and review the results with {{ fraud_review_audience }}.
controls.objective: The organization has considered how fraud could compromise its systems and commitments, and each identified scenario has a documented response.
controls.guidance: Perform it as a dedicated section of the annual risk assessment (OGRL-RM-02) and record scenarios in the same register with a fraud tag. Typical SaaS scenarios: an engineer altering production data, an admin granting themselves access, payment redirection through a vendor change request, and executives bypassing change approval. Evidence: the fraud section of the assessment and its review record.

fraud_review_audience.label: Fraud risk review audience
fraud_review_audience.value: executive leadership and the board or its designated committee

mappings.summary: Fraud and insider-misuse scenarios are one category of threat identified in a system risk assessment.
Directly addresses consideration of fraud potential in risk assessment; the criterion's broader scope is not claimed.

controls.name: Risk Treatment Tracking
controls.summary: Record a treatment decision, owner, and target date for each risk above tolerance, with approved and time-bound risk acceptances.
controls.statement: For each risk rated above {{ risk_tolerance_threshold }}, record a treatment decision (mitigate, transfer, avoid, or accept), an owner, and a target date. Risk acceptances require documented approval by {{ risk_acceptance_authority }} and expire after {{ acceptance_duration }}. Review treatment progress and acceptances {{ treatment_review_frequency }}.
controls.objective: Every risk outside tolerance has an accountable, tracked response consistent with leadership's risk appetite.
controls.guidance: Track treatment in the risk register or link register entries to tickets. Mitigation plans should reference the controls being added or strengthened; transfer should reference the contract or insurance policy.
