Evidence: register entries with decisions, approvals, and review dates.

risk_acceptance_authority.label: Risk acceptance authority
risk_acceptance_authority.value: the CEO for high risks and the security leader for others

risk_tolerance_threshold.label: Risk tolerance threshold
risk_tolerance_threshold.value: the tolerance level defined in the risk methodology

mappings.summary: Responds to risk assessment results in line with risk tolerance; responses to audit and monitoring findings are covered by deficiency tracking.
Determining and tracking how each identified risk will be managed.
Treatment decisions mitigate identified risks, including risks of business disruption.

controls.name: Significant Change Risk Evaluation
controls.summary: Evaluate security risk before significant changes take effect and update the risk register accordingly.
controls.statement: Before a significant change takes effect, including {{ significant_changes }}, evaluate its effect on security risk and on existing controls, document the evaluation, update the risk register, and obtain approval from {{ change_risk_approver }}.
controls.objective: Risk and control impacts of significant changes are understood and addressed before the changes take effect.
controls.guidance: Trigger the evaluation from the architecture review or design-doc template, vendor onboarding, and leadership or legal change processes. A short structured note (what changed, new risks, affected controls, decision) linked to the register entry is sufficient. Routine code changes are covered by change management, not this control.

significant_changes.label: Changes requiring risk evaluation
significant_changes.value: new products or major features, architecture or hosting changes, new critical vendors, acquisitions, leadership changes, and new regulatory obligations

mappings.summary: Covers the change-driven update of the risk assessment; periodic updates are covered by periodic risk assessment.
Evaluates internal and external changes for their effect on risk and controls.

controls.name: Cyber Insurance
controls.summary: Maintain cyber insurance sized to the organization's risk and review its adequacy at each renewal.
controls.statement: Maintain cyber liability insurance with limits of at least {{ coverage_minimum }} that covers incident response costs, business interruption, and third-party liability arising from security incidents. Review coverage adequacy against the risk register and customer contractual requirements {{ insurance_review_frequency }}.
controls.objective: The financial impact of a significant security incident is partially transferred, consistent with risk treatment decisions and customer commitments.
controls.guidance: Many enterprise customer contracts specify minimum cyber coverage; record those in the commitments register (OGRL-GV-07). Note insurer requirements such as MFA or EDR that become implicit control commitments, and include the carrier's breach hotline in the incident response plan. Evidence: the current certificate of insurance and the renewal review record.

coverage_minimum.label: Minimum aggregate coverage limit
coverage_minimum.value: USD 2,000,000 or the highest amount required by customer contracts

mappings.summary: Insurance is a risk transfer mechanism for losses from business disruption.

controls.name: Secure Development Lifecycle
controls.summary: Maintain a documented SDLC that builds security activities, roles, and design principles into every phase.
controls.statement: Maintain a documented secure development lifecycle that defines required security activities for design, implementation, testing, release, and maintenance, requires threat modeling for {{ threat_model_triggers }}, applies {{ secure_design_principles }}, assigns security responsibilities to named roles, and is reviewed and approved by {{ sdlc_owner }} {{ sdlc_review_frequency }}.
controls.objective: Ensure security is designed into systems consistently rather than added after release.
controls.guidance: Keep the SDLC as a short engineering handbook page that links to the concrete gates: design review template, code review (OGRL-SD-02), automated scanning (OGRL-SD-03), branch protection (OGRL-SD-04), and change testing (OGRL-CM-07). Record approval with a dated sign-off. Reference OWASP SAMM or NIST SSDF if a maturity model is helpful.

sdlc_owner.label: SDLC approval authority
sdlc_owner.value: the head of engineering and the security lead

secure_design_principles.label: Secure design principles
secure_design_principles.value: least privilege, defense in depth, secure defaults, and attack-surface minimization

threat_model_triggers.label: Work requiring threat modeling
threat_model_triggers.value: new services, new external integrations, and major architecture changes

mappings.summary: Defines secure design principles and development techniques and requires threat modeling for developed software; architectural designs and engineering principles for the wider CUI environment are not covered.
A documented SDLC with security activities in each phase satisfies SA-3(a).
The SDLC assigns security responsibilities to named roles, addressing SA-3(b).
Threat modeling integrates risk analysis into development, partly addressing SA-3(d).
The SDLC names secure design principles to apply, supplying the SA-8 principles; application across all lifecycle stages is broader.
The SDLC is a technology general control over development, contributing to CC5.2.
A secure SDLC governs how changes are designed and developed, contributing to CC8.1.

controls.name: Peer Code Review
controls.summary: Require security-qualified review of changes to security-sensitive code before merge.
controls.statement: Require every pull request that modifies {{ security_sensitive_code }} to be reviewed and approved by {{ security_code_reviewer }} using {{ code_review_techniques }} before merge, enforced through code-owner rules in the source control platform.
controls.objective: Catch security defects in high-risk code paths that general peer review and automated scanning may miss.
controls.guidance: Map security-sensitive paths in a CODEOWNERS file to a security reviewer group and enable the require-code-owner-review branch protection setting. General independent peer review of all production changes is covered by OGRL-CM-01; this control adds security-focused review for high-risk code.

code_review_techniques.label: Security code review technique
code_review_techniques.value: the organization's secure code review checklist covering OWASP Top 10 weakness classes

security_code_reviewer.label: Security code reviewer
security_code_reviewer.value: a designated security code owner other than the author

security_sensitive_code.label: Security-sensitive code requiring security review
security_sensitive_code.value: authentication, authorization, cryptography, session management, payment, and tenant-isolation code paths

mappings.summary: Checklist-driven manual review of designated security-sensitive code satisfies SA-11(4).
Security review of high-risk code before merge is part of authorizing and testing changes under CC8.1.

controls.name: Static Analysis and Dependency Scanning
controls.summary: Run SAST, secret scanning, and dependency analysis on every pull request and block merges on serious findings.
controls.statement: Run static application security testing, secret scanning, and software composition analysis on every pull request to {{ scanned_repositories }}, block merge on unresolved findings rated {{ blocking_severity }} or above unless an exception is approved by {{ scan_exception_approver }}, and retain scan results with the change record.
controls.objective: Prevent common code flaws, leaked secrets, and known-vulnerable dependencies from being merged.
controls.guidance: Use CI-integrated tools such as CodeQL or Semgrep, GitHub secret scanning with push protection, and Dependabot or Snyk, configured as required status checks. Track approved exceptions with an expiry date. Ongoing scanning of deployed images and dependencies is covered by OGRL-VM-01.

scanned_repositories.label: Repositories subject to scanning
scanned_repositories.value: all repositories that build or deploy production code or infrastructure

mappings.summary: Static analysis on every pull request with retained results meets SA-11(1), with secret and dependency scanning added.
Pre-merge scanning identifies vulnerabilities introduced by new code, overlapping CC7.1 detection activities.
Automated security testing gates contribute to testing changes before implementation under CC8.1.

controls.name: Source Control and Branch Protection
controls.summary: Keep all production code and configuration in managed source control with enforced branch protection.
controls.statement: Maintain {{ versioned_assets }} in {{ source_control_platform }}, enforce branch protection on {{ protected_branches }} that blocks direct pushes, force-pushes, and deletion and requires an approved pull request with passing checks to merge, and verify protection settings on all production repositories {{ branch_protection_review_frequency }}.
controls.objective: Ensure every production change is versioned, attributable, and can only enter protected branches through the approved workflow.
controls.guidance: Apply organization-level rulesets so new repositories inherit protection, disallow administrator bypass, and require SSO for platform access. Script a quarterly export of branch protection settings across repositories (for example via the GitHub API) as evidence. Review content requirements are covered by OGRL-CM-01 and OGRL-SD-02.

source_control_platform.label: Source control platform
source_control_platform.value: the organization's SSO-enforced source control platform

versioned_assets.label: Assets kept under source control
versioned_assets.value: application source code, infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD pipeline definitions, and deployment configuration

mappings.summary: Versioning all production assets and protecting branches controls the integrity of changes to configuration items per SA-10(b).
Branch protection ensures only approved pull requests enter release branches, partly enforcing SA-10(c).
Protected, versioned source control enforces the authorized path for changes under CC8.1.

controls.name: Processing Specifications and Data Definitions
controls.summary: Document and maintain versioned specifications of inputs, processing rules, and outputs for in-scope systems.
controls.statement: Document, for each in-scope processing system, the input data definitions, accepted formats and value ranges, processing rules, and expected outputs in version-controlled specifications, update them with every change that alters processing behavior, have them reviewed by {{ spec_owner }} {{ spec_review_frequency }}, and make them available to {{ spec_audience }}.
controls.objective: Provide a single accurate reference for how each system is expected to process data, so processing can be built, tested, and verified against it.
controls.guidance: Machine-readable specifications work best: OpenAPI or GraphQL schemas, JSON Schema or protobuf data contracts, and database schema migrations, supplemented by short design notes for business rules. Generate customer-facing API documentation from the same source. Input validation (OGRL-SD-06) and output validation (OGRL-SD-08) should enforce these definitions.

spec_audience.label: Specification audience
spec_audience.value: engineering, support, and customers through published API documentation

spec_owner.label: Specification owner
spec_owner.value: the product or engineering owner of each system

mappings.summary: Data definitions identify the information types a system processes, loosely overlapping PL-2(a)(5).
Processing specifications are distributed to defined audiences, overlapping SA-5(d) distribution of system documentation.
Documented data definitions and processing specifications support PI1.1.

controls.name: Input Validation
controls.summary: Validate all external inputs against defined schemas before processing and reject or quarantine invalid data.
controls.statement: Validate inputs received through {{ validated_input_channels }} against defined schemas for type, length, format, and range before processing, reject or quarantine invalid inputs and log the reason, and verify validation behavior with automated tests in the CI pipeline.
controls.objective: Ensure only complete, well-formed, and expected data enters processing, protecting both data accuracy and the application from injection attacks.
controls.guidance: Enforce validation at the API boundary with schema validators generated from the specification (for example OpenAPI request validation, zod, or pydantic). Use allow-list validation, parameterized queries, and size limits on uploads. Batch imports should report rejected rows back to the submitter.

validated_input_channels.label: Input channels subject to validation
validated_input_channels.value: public APIs, user interface forms, file uploads, webhooks, and batch data imports

mappings.summary: Schema-based validity checks on named input channels satisfy SI-10.
Validating inputs for completeness and accuracy before processing contributes to PI1.2.

controls.name: Error Handling
controls.summary: Return safe error messages, keep error detail restricted, and never silently drop failed transactions.
controls.statement: Implement application error handling that returns messages giving users enough information to correct the problem without exposing stack traces, internal identifiers, queries, or system details, records detailed error information only in logs accessible to {{ error_detail_roles }}, and rolls back or routes failed transactions to {{ error_queue }} for retry or correction so that no processing failure is silently discarded.
controls.objective: Ensure processing errors are corrected rather than lost, without leaking information useful to an attacker.
controls.guidance: Use a global exception handler that maps exceptions to generic responses with a correlation ID. Disable framework debug modes in production. Wrap multi-step writes in transactions and configure dead-letter queues with alerting on depth for asynchronous consumers. Reconciliation of processed volumes is covered by OGRL-LM-05.

error_detail_roles.label: Roles permitted to view detailed errors

error_queue.label: Failed transaction handling destination
error_queue.value: a monitored dead-letter or error queue

mappings.summary: User-facing errors that aid correction without revealing exploitable details satisfy SI-11(a).
Detailed error information is restricted to defined roles per SI-11(b).
Rolling back or queuing failed transactions for correction supports complete and accurate processing under PI1.3.

controls.name: Output Validation and Distribution
controls.summary: Validate system outputs before release and deliver them only to authorized recipients.
controls.statement: Validate outputs from {{ validated_output_sources }} against expected schemas, record counts, or control totals before release, deliver outputs only to authorized recipients through {{ output_delivery_channels }}, and hold, investigate, and correct any output that fails validation before it is redistributed.
controls.objective: Ensure outputs are complete, accurate, and reach only their intended recipients.
controls.guidance: Apply response schema validation in API tests, compare export row counts with source query counts, and enforce tenant scoping on download and API endpoints. Failed validations should block publication and page the owning team.

output_delivery_channels.label: Authorized output delivery channels
output_delivery_channels.value: authenticated APIs, tenant-scoped downloads, and encrypted transfer channels

validated_output_sources.label: Outputs subject to validation
validated_output_sources.value: customer-facing reports, data exports, outbound data feeds, and API responses with defined schemas

mappings.summary: Validating outputs against expected content meets SI-15, with authorized distribution added.
Output validation and restricted delivery support complete, accurate, and properly distributed outputs under PI1.4.

controls.name: Vendor Inventory and Risk Tiering
controls.summary: Keep an inventory of vendors that touch in-scope systems or data, each with an owner and a risk tier.
controls.statement: Maintain an inventory of every third party that stores, processes, or accesses customer data or supports in-scope systems, recording for each its internal owner, services provided, data shared, and a risk tier assigned using {{ tiering_criteria }}; add each vendor to the inventory before production use or data sharing, and review the full inventory {{ inventory_review_frequency }}.
controls.objective: Know which third parties the service depends on and how much risk each one carries, so oversight effort can be proportionate.
controls.guidance: Seed the inventory from finance and expense data, SSO application catalogs, and infrastructure-as-code provider lists to catch shadow vendors. Flag subservice organizations that will be carved out of the SOC 2 report. The risk tier drives due diligence depth (OGRL-TP-02) and monitoring cadence (OGRL-TP-04).

tiering_criteria.label: Risk tiering criteria
tiering_criteria.value: the sensitivity of data shared, level of system access, and operational criticality of the service

mappings.summary: Assigning an internal owner to each external service documents oversight responsibility; broader user roles and responsibilities are not addressed.
A tiered vendor inventory is a core input to supply chain risk planning but is not itself a supply chain risk management plan.
Identifying vendors and tiering their risk is the starting point for vendor risk management under CC9.2.

controls.name: Vendor Security Due Diligence
controls.summary: Assess the security and privacy posture of higher-risk vendors and approve the risk before signing or sharing data.
controls.statement: Before onboarding any vendor rated {{ diligence_tiers }}, and again when the services or data shared materially change, assess its security and privacy posture using {{ assessment_evidence }}, document findings and any accepted risks, and obtain approval from {{ vendor_risk_approver }} before contract signature or data sharing.
controls.objective: Avoid taking on vendors whose security posture is inconsistent with the organization's commitments to customers.
controls.guidance: Scale the assessment to the tier: an independent assurance report review for critical vendors, a standard questionnaire for moderate ones, and a lightweight checklist for low-risk tools. Route approvals through procurement so contracts cannot be signed without security sign-off. Periodic reassessment after onboarding is covered by OGRL-TP-04.

assessment_evidence.label: Due diligence evidence
assessment_evidence.value: a current SOC 2 Type II report, ISO/IEC 27001 certificate, or completed security questionnaire

mappings.summary: Pre-onboarding and change-triggered supplier assessments address SR-6; periodic reassessment is handled by OGRL-TP-04.
Assessing vendor security before engagement is a key vendor risk management activity under CC9.2.

controls.name: Vendor Contract Security and Privacy Requirements
controls.summary: Put security, confidentiality, privacy, and breach notification obligations in writing before sharing sensitive data with a vendor.
controls.statement: Execute a written agreement with every vendor that will store, process, or access confidential or personal data before sharing that data, including security and confidentiality obligations, data protection terms that restrict use to the contracted purpose, notification of security incidents or unauthorized disclosures affecting organizational data within {{ breach_notification_window }}, disclosure of subprocessors, return or deletion of data at termination, and the right to obtain {{ assurance_rights }}.
controls.objective: Make vendors contractually accountable for protecting the organization's and its customers' data.
controls.guidance: Maintain a standard security addendum and data processing agreement; legal tracks deviations and security approves them. Align the vendor notification window with the organization's own customer notification commitments. Record contract status in the vendor inventory so missing agreements are visible.

assurance_rights.label: Assurance rights required from vendors
assurance_rights.value: independent audit reports or security questionnaire responses at least annually

mappings.summary: Contractual security, privacy, and responsibility-allocation terms overlap SA-4 acquisition requirements, which also address system development and assurance criteria not covered here.
Contract terms are one control employed to limit harm from supply chain events.
Vendor confidentiality and deletion obligations help protect confidential information under C1.1.
Contractual security requirements are a primary means of managing vendor risk under CC9.2.
Data protection terms bind vendors with access to personal information to privacy obligations relevant to P6.4.
Required vendor notification of unauthorized disclosures supports P6.5.

controls.name: Ongoing Vendor Monitoring and SOC Report Review
controls.summary: Periodically review assurance reports for critical vendors and act on exceptions and complementary controls.
controls.statement: For each vendor rated {{ monitored_tiers }}, obtain and review {{ assurance_evidence }} {{ monitoring_frequency }}; evaluate reported exceptions, coverage gaps, and complementary user entity controls the organization must operate; track remediation of identified issues; and record the review outcome and any risk acceptance.
controls.objective: Detect deterioration in vendor security posture and confirm the organization performs its share of vendor-dependent controls.
controls.guidance: Track report periods and request bridge letters when coverage lapses. Map each relevant complementary user entity control to an internal control or owner. Subservice organizations carved out of the organization's own SOC 2 report need this review as evidence of monitoring. Also monitor public breach disclosures for critical vendors.

assurance_evidence.label: Vendor assurance evidence reviewed
assurance_evidence.value: the vendor's most recent SOC 2 Type II report, ISO/IEC 27001 certificate, or equivalent independent assessment

monitored_tiers.label: Vendor tiers subject to periodic monitoring

mappings.summary: Periodic review of vendor assurance reports is the method used to monitor provider control compliance on an ongoing basis.
Evaluating third-party assurance reports is a form of ongoing evaluation of controls relevant to CC4.1.
Ongoing review of vendor assurance reports is a vendor monitoring activity under CC9.2.

controls.name: Vulnerability Scanning and SLA-Driven Remediation
controls.summary: Scan infrastructure, containers, and dependencies continuously for vulnerabilities and remediate findings within risk-based SLAs.
controls.statement: Scan in-scope infrastructure, container images, and application dependencies for vulnerabilities {{ scan_cadence }}, remediate confirmed findings within {{ remediation_sla }}, and share advisories with {{ advisory_audience }}.
controls.objective: Identify and remediate exploitable software flaws and misconfigurations before adversaries leverage them.
controls.guidance: Combine authenticated infrastructure scanning with CI/CD dependency/container scanning and track open vulnerabilities in an issue tracker with explicit SLA due dates.

advisory_audience.label: Internal advisory recipients
advisory_audience.value: engineering service owners and platform security leads

remediation_sla.label: Vulnerability remediation SLA
remediation_sla.value: 15 days for critical and 30 days for high severity findings

scan_cadence.label: Vulnerability scanning frequency
scan_cadence.value: at least weekly and on every release

tests.name: Verify Vulnerability Scan Cadence and SLA Compliance
tests.description: Confirm vulnerability scans completed within the configured cadence and no confirmed critical or high findings remain open past their remediation SLA.

mappings.summary: Scheduled and per-release scanning meets the periodic scan objectives; scanning when new vulnerabilities emerge depends on the cadence value.
Scanning identifies vulnerabilities and severity-based SLAs drive risk-ranked remediation, though lower severities lack a defined treatment.
Continuous vulnerability scanning and SLA remediation satisfy SP 800-171 03.11.02.
Scheduled infrastructure and release vulnerability scanning satisfies NIST RA-5(a).
Risk-based vulnerability remediation SLAs directly satisfy NIST RA-5(d).
Sharing vulnerability advisories with service owners satisfies NIST RA-5(e).
Continuous vulnerability scanning identifies technical risks informing SOC 2 CC3.2.
Vulnerability scanning and SLA remediation satisfy SOC 2 CC7.1 detection obligations.

controls.name: Flaw Remediation and Patching
controls.summary: Apply security updates within defined timeframes after testing, through the normal change process.
controls.statement: Install security-relevant updates for operating systems, container base images, language runtimes, and third-party dependencies within {{ patch_sla }} of vendor release, test each update in a non-production environment before production deployment, and deploy updates through the standard change management process.
controls.objective: Close known software flaws quickly without destabilizing production.
controls.guidance: Automate update pull requests (for example Dependabot or Renovate), rebuild images on base-image releases, and enable managed-service auto-patching with maintenance windows. Track patch age as a metric against the SLA. Vulnerability identification and scanning is covered by OGRL-VM-01.

patch_sla.label: Security update installation SLA
patch_sla.value: 14 days for critical, 30 days for high, and 90 days for other security updates

mappings.summary: Patching within severity-based SLAs remediates many vulnerabilities but not those fixed by configuration or identified elsewhere.
Patching within defined SLAs meets the flaw correction objectives; identifying and reporting flaws within set times fall to other controls.
Applying security updates corrects system flaws; identification and reporting are handled by vulnerability scanning.
Updates are tested in non-production before production deployment per SI-2(b).
A defined installation timeframe for security updates satisfies SI-2(c).
Patches flow through the standard change process, incorporating flaw remediation into configuration management per SI-2(d).
Timely patching remediates the vulnerabilities that CC7.1 monitoring identifies.
Patches are tested and deployed as controlled changes, contributing to CC8.1.

controls.name: Malware Protection
controls.summary: Run centrally managed, auto-updating anti-malware or EDR on endpoints and hosts and act on detections.
controls.statement: Deploy centrally managed anti-malware or endpoint detection and response on {{ malware_protected_assets }}, keep engines and signatures automatically updated, scan files in real time on download, open, or execution and perform full scans {{ malware_scan_frequency }}, automatically {{ malware_response_action }} detected malicious code and alert {{ malware_alert_recipients }}, and verify agent coverage {{ malware_coverage_review_frequency }}.
controls.objective: Detect and contain malicious code on systems that can execute it.
controls.guidance: Use MDM to deploy and lock the EDR agent on laptops, and runtime protection or EDR on general-purpose production hosts. Immutable containers rely on image scanning and least functionality (OGRL-CM-08) rather than agents. Scan customer-uploaded files before processing where the product accepts uploads. Compare the EDR agent list with the device inventory monthly.

malware_protected_assets.label: Assets requiring malware protection
malware_protected_assets.value: workforce endpoints and production hosts running general-purpose operating systems

mappings.summary: Managed anti-malware on designated assets meets 3.14.2 and also covers updating and scanning.
Automatic engine and signature updates meet 3.14.4 within a broader anti-malware control.
Scheduled full scans and real-time scanning on download, open, or execution meet 3.14.5.
Endpoint and host anti-malware provides detection and eradication, though not necessarily at every system entry and exit point required by SI-3(a).
Automatic engine and signature updates satisfy SI-3(b).
Real-time scanning plus scheduled full scans meet SI-3(c)(1).
Automatic block or quarantine with alerts to defined recipients meets SI-3(c)(2).
Anti-malware detection and quarantine help prevent and detect malicious software under CC6.8.

controls.name: Security Alerts and Threat Intelligence
controls.summary: Receive external security advisories, triage those affecting in-scope technology, and drive required actions.
controls.statement: Subscribe to security advisories and threat intelligence from {{ advisory_sources }}, triage each advisory affecting in-scope technologies within {{ advisory_triage_sla }}, disseminate actionable advisories to {{ advisory_recipients }}, and track required actions to completion in the issue tracker.
controls.objective: Learn about relevant new threats and vulnerabilities promptly and ensure they result in action.
controls.guidance: Route vendor security bulletins, the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities feed, and GitHub security advisories into a shared channel or ticket queue owned by security. Record a triage decision on each relevant advisory. Remediation timelines follow OGRL-VM-01 and OGRL-VM-02.

advisory_recipients.label: Advisory dissemination recipients
advisory_recipients.value: affected service owners and the engineering on-call channel

advisory_sources.label: Advisory and threat intelligence sources
advisory_sources.value: vendors of in-scope software and cloud services, CISA (including the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog), and GitHub security advisories

mappings.summary: Monitoring advisories, triaging them, and tracking actions to completion meets 3.14.3.
Ongoing subscriptions to named advisory sources satisfy SI-5(a).
Actionable advisories are disseminated to defined internal recipients per SI-5(c).

controls.name: Penetration Testing

controls.objective: Find exploitable weaknesses that automated scanning misses and confirm they are fixed.
controls.guidance: Define rules of engagement and scope in a statement of work, include authenticated testing of multi-tenant isolation, and import findings into the vulnerability tracker. Keep the executive summary and retest letter as evidence; many customers will request them.

controls.name: Endpoint and Mobile Device Access Requirements
controls.summary: Allow access to company systems only from managed devices that meet defined security requirements.
controls.statement: Permit access to organizational systems and data only from laptops and mobile devices enrolled in {{ device_management_platform }} that meet {{ device_security_requirements }}, enforce compliance with device-posture checks at sign-on, and block access from non-compliant devices and revoke access and remotely wipe company data on lost or stolen devices within {{ device_revocation_sla }} of report.
controls.objective: Ensure company data is only accessed from devices that can protect it, including outside the office.
controls.guidance: Combine MDM (for example Jamf, Intune, or Kandji) with identity-provider device trust or conditional access so only compliant devices receive SSO sessions. Use app protection policies or work profiles for personal mobile devices. Evidence is the device compliance policy, the IdP conditional-access rule, and a compliance report.

device_management_platform.value: the organization's mobile device management (MDM) platform

device_security_requirements.label: Device security requirements
device_security_requirements.value: full-disk encryption, screen lock after 15 minutes or less, a supported OS with automatic updates, and remote-wipe capability

Device-posture checks authorize only compliant devices to connect per AC-19(b).

controls.name: Collaborative Computing Device Controls
controls.summary: Prevent remote activation of cameras, microphones, and other collaborative devices and show users when they are in use.
controls.statement: Identify {{ collaborative_devices }} on in-scope systems in the asset inventory, configure them so they cannot be activated remotely except for {{ remote_activation_exceptions }}, ensure each provides an explicit indication of use, such as an indicator light or on-screen notice, to users physically present at the device whenever it is active, and verify these settings {{ collab_config_review_frequency }}.
controls.objective: Collaborative computing devices are known, cannot be switched on remotely outside approved exceptions, and always show users nearby when they are in use.
controls.guidance: Collaborative computing devices include built-in and USB webcams, microphones, conference-room video systems, and interactive whiteboards. Use MDM privacy profiles (for example macOS PPPC or Windows privacy policies) so only approved conferencing apps can use the camera and microphone and remote-support or management tools cannot turn them on. Rely on hardware-wired camera lights and operating system in-use indicators, and do not disable them. In conferencing tenants, turn off far-end camera control and any feature that lets remote parties start a device without a local user acting. Room systems that only start when a participant places or accepts a call fall within the default exception. Keep the device list in the asset inventory and spot-check settings through MDM compliance reports.

collaborative_devices.label: Collaborative computing devices in scope
collaborative_devices.value: cameras and microphones on workforce endpoints, conference-room video systems, and networked interactive whiteboards

remote_activation_exceptions.label: Permitted exceptions to the remote activation prohibition
remote_activation_exceptions.value: dedicated video conferencing systems that activate only when a participant in the room places or accepts a call

mappings.summary: Inventorying collaborative devices, blocking remote activation, and showing in-use indicators meets 3.13.12.

Requiring an explicit in-use indicator for people at the device meets SC-15(b).

controls.name: Mobile Code Control
controls.summary: Define which mobile code may run, block the rest through managed settings, and monitor its use.
controls.statement: Define and document acceptable and unacceptable mobile code and mobile code technologies; enforce the definitions on workforce endpoints and in-scope systems through centrally managed settings that {{ mobile_code_restrictions }}; permit exceptions only with documented approval from {{ mobile_code_exception_approver }}; monitor mobile code use and blocked execution through {{ mobile_code_monitoring_sources }}; and review the definitions and settings {{ mobile_code_review_frequency }}.
controls.objective: Only mobile code and mobile code technologies the organization has defined as acceptable run on in-scope systems, and their use is monitored.
controls.guidance: Mobile code is software obtained from remote systems and run locally without explicit installation, such as JavaScript, VBScript, Office macros, PDF scripts, browser extensions, Java applets, and ActiveX. Record which of these are acceptable and which are prohibited in the endpoint configuration standard. Use MDM or group policy to block macros in files from the internet, allow only signed or trusted-location macros, manage browser extensions by allowlist, and disable legacy plug-ins. Use EDR and secure web gateway or DNS filtering logs to monitor script execution and blocked downloads, and send block events to the logging platform. For web applications the organization operates, a Content Security Policy limits which scripts browsers will run.

mobile_code_monitoring_sources.label: Sources used to monitor mobile code use
mobile_code_monitoring_sources.value: endpoint detection and response telemetry, browser management reports, and web filtering or secure web gateway logs

mobile_code_restrictions.label: Technical restrictions enforcing the mobile code definitions
mobile_code_restrictions.value: block Office macros in files from the internet and unsigned macros, allow browser extensions only from an approved list, disable Java applets, ActiveX, and other legacy plug-ins, and disable JavaScript in PDF readers

mobile_code_review_frequency.label: Mobile code definitions and settings review frequency

mappings.summary: Defining, enforcing, and monitoring allowed mobile code meets 3.13.13.

controls.name: VoIP Control and Monitoring
controls.summary: Restrict VoIP to approved, securely configured services and log and review their use.
controls.statement: Permit only {{ approved_voip_services }} for Voice over Internet Protocol calling on organizational systems; configure them with {{ voip_security_settings }}; restrict unapproved VoIP applications on managed endpoints; collect administrative audit logs and call detail records from approved services in the central logging platform; and review VoIP usage and configuration for anomalies {{ voip_review_frequency }}.
controls.objective: Voice over IP use is limited to approved, securely configured services, and their use is logged and reviewed.
controls.guidance: Most small contractors use a cloud calling or unified communications service rather than on-premises PBX equipment. Choose a service approved for the data it will carry; if calls, chat, or recordings may contain CUI, the service is in assessment scope. Manage desk phones and softphone clients through the service's admin console and MDM, and block consumer calling apps on managed endpoints where practical. Turn on admin audit logs and call detail records, forward them to the logging platform, and look for unusual international calling, toll fraud, new external federation, or sign-ins from unexpected locations.

approved_voip_services.value: the organization's approved unified communications or cloud calling service and the desk phones and softphone clients it manages

voip_review_frequency.label: VoIP usage and configuration review frequency

voip_security_settings.label: Required VoIP security settings
voip_security_settings.value: single sign-on with multi-factor authentication for users and administrators, encrypted signaling and media, external federation and international calling restricted to approved uses, and administrative audit logging enabled
